newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius leading shares continue climb.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius leading shares continue climb.

text.p: Leading shares at the Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM) continued to climb on Monday, again propelled by news that a new $60 million country fund would be a future buyer in the market, brokers said.
SEM market index Semdex gained 3.46 points to 313.55 in lower volume of 1.99 million rupees on 112,632 shares from 10.42 million rupees on 434,344 shares last Friday.
"Investors are still encouraged by the Port Louis Fund. You do not often hear that a new country fund will get in the market with $15 million to spend," one broker said.
On Friday, Semdex rose for the first time after 19 straight trading sessions of a downward slide after Mauritian Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam announced the setting up of the fund.

Out of the $60 million, $15 million have been earmarked for investments in the SEM while the remaining $45 million will be used to acquire equity stakes in state linked enterprises such as Air Mauritius, State Bank of Mauritius, Mauritius Telecom and the State Investment Corporation.
The Port Louis Fund creation shook up the Mauritian bourse which for the past couple of months was depressed on political uncertainty and a long absence of a finance minister.
Leading shares continued to climb as they were seen to be most likely on the Port Louis Fund's shopping list.

Mauritius Commercial Bank was up a rupee to 72 on 4,100 shares but State Bank of Mauritius was unchanged at 8.60 rupees on 300 shares. National Investment Trust (NIT) gained 10 cents to 10.90 rupees on 5,640 shares and Mauritius Development Investment Trust added 20 cents to 7.0 rupees on 1,500 shares.

Sugar-based Mon Tresor Mon Desert was 1.10 rupees higher to 34.50 rupees on 5,050 shares. Conglomerates Rogers rose 50 cents to 84 rupees but attracted no trading volume and Ireland Blyth surged by 60 cents to 12.80 rupees on 130 shares.
New Mauritius Hotels gained 20 cents to 27.80 rupees on 21,685 shares and Air Mauritius rose 1.0 to 49 on 410 shares.
